question: An investigator is studying the principles of cell-to-cell signaling of the autonomic nervous system. It is found that the adrenal medulla has receptors that, when activated, result in the immediate opening of Na+, Ca2+, and K+ channels, which subsequently leads to the secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine. These receptors are structurally most similar to which of the following receptors?

options.opb: Alpha 1 receptors of the bladder neck
options.opd: D2 receptors of the basal ganglia
options.ope: NM receptors of the quadriceps femoris muscle

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Adrenal medulla receptors activation -> Opening of Na+, Ca2+, and K+ channels -> Secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine -> Similarity to Alpha 1 receptors of the bladder neck -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Adrenal medulla receptors activation -> Opening of Na+, Ca2+, and K+ channels -> Secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine -> Similarity to NM receptors of the quadriceps femoris muscle -> 85%
analysis: The receptors in the adrenal medulla that lead to the secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine upon activation are most similar to the NM receptors of the quadriceps femoris muscle. These receptors are involved in the neuromuscular junction and play a role in muscle contraction, similar to the role of adrenal medulla receptors in triggering the release of catecholamines.
